headline: 10 injured as AC explodes at Gulistan salon in Old Dhaka
summary: Customers and staff at 'Arman Hair Cutting' salon were burned when an air conditioner exploded on Tuesday night.
details: An air conditioner explosion at a salon in the Alu Bazar area of Gulistan left 10 people injured, including both customers and staff members.
The incident occurred on Tuesday night at a salon named 'Arman Hair Cutting'.
According to Resident Surgeon Shaon Bin Rahman of the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, nine of the victims are currently receiving treatment at the facility.
Among the customers, Md. Faruk suffered 50% burns, while Rinku (21%), Roni (10%), Jasim (8%), and Rafiq (12%) were also injured.
The staff members affected include Samshed (15%), Raju (18%), Pappu (18%), Arman (15%), and Sakib, who suffered 1% burns.
Sakib was discharged after receiving primary treatment, while the other nine remain admitted for further care.
caption:
10 people burned after an air conditioner exploded inside a hair salon in Old Dhaka.

An air conditioner explosion at a salon in the Alu Bazar area of Gulistan left 10 people injured, including both customers and staff members.

The incident occurred on Tuesday night at a salon named 'Arman Hair Cutting'.

According to Resident Surgeon Shaon Bin Rahman of the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, nine of the victims are currently receiving treatment at the facility.

Among the customers, Md. Faruk suffered 50% burns, while Rinku (21%), Roni (10%), Jasim (8%), and Rafiq (12%) were also injured.

The staff members affected include Samshed (15%), Raju (18%), Pappu (18%), Arman (15%), and Sakib, who suffered 1% burns.

Sakib was discharged after receiving primary treatment, while the other nine remain admitted for further care.

headline_marked: Tk 890 crore loss: [[7 lakh people affected by floods]] in Cox's Bazar
headline: Tk 890 crore loss: 7 lakh people affected by floods in Cox's Bazar
summary: Heavy rainfall and flash floods caused massive damage to homes, roads, and agriculture across 70 unions of the district.
details: Nine days of torrential rain and flash floods from the hills have devastated Cox's Bazar, affecting at least 7 lakh people. Initial assessments by the district administration estimate losses of Tk 890 crore across seven sectors, including housing, roads, agriculture, and fisheries.

The disaster struck between July 4 and July 12, with 823mm of rain falling in just nine days—nearly the entire average monthly rainfall for July. The floods and accompanying landslides claimed 31 lives, including 15 Rohingya refugees.

Infrastructure has been severely hit, with over 350 kilometers of roads damaged in the Chakaria area alone, leaving many residents stranded. In Pekua, 95% of the area was submerged, and hundreds of families remain waterlogged in low-lying villages.

Agriculture and fisheries suffered heavily, with over 10,000 acres of crops submerged and nearly 4,000 ponds and 453 shrimp farms destroyed. This has resulted in losses of approximately Tk 46.22 crore for fish farmers alone.

The district administration has distributed thousands of dry food packets and hundreds of metric tons of rice, but a significant shortage remains. There is an urgent need for more food, cash aid, water purification tablets, and corrugated iron sheets for damaged homes.

Local officials noted that the floodwaters receded more slowly in the newly formed Matamuhuri Upazila because influential locals had blocked sluice gates with fishing nets. Guards have since been posted to keep the gates open and facilitate drainage.

7 lakh people affected and Tk 890 crore in losses. Cox's Bazar has been devastated by unprecedented rainfall and flash floods.

Agriculture and fisheries suffered heavily, with over 10,000 acres of crops submerged and nearly 4,000 ponds and 453 shrimp farms destroyed. This has resulted in losses of approximately Tk 46.22 crore for fish farmers alone.

The district administration has distributed thousands of dry food packets and hundreds of metric tons of rice, but a significant shortage remains. There is an urgent need for more food, cash aid, water purification tablets, and corrugated iron sheets for damaged homes.
